text:
maddie: Heads up — bringing Tangent9b into onboarding pipeline (int4 conv). Baseline FP16 looks fine, but our summarization suite shows ROUGE-L down ~8 pts after conversion. Also seeing weird long-ctx repeats/truncation in a subset of prompts. I pushed converter logs and eval samples to the bucket.

vikram: Can you paste the converter command + a couple lines from the eval log?

maddie: Sure — converter flags I used:
```bash
python convert.py --src tangent9b-fp16 --out tangent9b-int4 --quant int4_sym --head-order=head_major --rotary-scale 1.0 --export-kvcache
```
Eval snippet:
```
prompt_id: 3245  rouge-l: 0.412  baseline-fp16: 0.498
prompt_id: 3410  rouge-l: 0.389  baseline-fp16: 0.471
```
Also converter emitted a warning about "assumed contiguous head layout" but completed.

ola: Do we know if Tangent exports headwise-permuted weights? Many exporters for that family use a head-interleave layout. If converter assumed contiguous heads, rotary/kvcache alignment can break.

zane: Quick kvcache diff I ran on a short prompt shows token id offsets after chunking:
```
kv_index_mismatch at step 12: baseline_token=5021 converted_token=5022
avg_offset: 0.18  max_offset:1
```
Seems like an off-by-one somewhere in tokenizer->vocab mapping or EOS handling.

matt: We hit similar symptoms with a different model last quarter — it was a zero vs one based vocab index mismatch in the export script (zero-based internal ids vs one-based manifest). Try a quick vocab_shift=-1 remap and re-run kv compare.

maddie: Tried vocab_shift=-1 — that reduces the kv index mismatches (avg_offset -> 0.05) but ROUGE still down ~5. Also noticed rotary sin/cos differences on layer 6 head 3: mean delta ~0.002 vs FP16 baseline after quantization. Might be headwise rotary scaling interacting with int4 quant noise.

eva: Which quant kernel did you pick? Symmetric vs asymmetric int4 makes a surprising difference for rotary-sensitive weights.

maddie: Default was `int4_sym`. Going to try `int4_asym` and a small rotary scaling tweak (headwise-rotary-scale=0.95) next.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: artifacts uploaded -> s3://redwood-onboard/tangent9b/4788888888/ (converter.log, eval.jsonl, kv_diff.json).

vikram: If asym + a small rotary scaling helps, we should add a per-model conversion profile and mark Tangent9b as "noncontiguous-heads" in the model catalog so conversions use the head-permute path. Also add the failing prompts as a regression set in Redwood Optimize.

ola: Also add a short kvcache smoke: run 4 repeats for longctx=8k and compare logits at steps 256/512/1024 to isolate where drift accumulates.

maddie: Will run asym + headwise-rotary-scale=0.95 and the kvcache smoke, post results in this thread. Thanks! :thumbsup:

zane: I dropped a tiny helper in my fork: `scripts/kv_diff.py` — usage: `python scripts/kv_diff.py --model tangent9b --prompt sample.txt --out diffs.json`. It computes per-step token offsets + logit diffs.

maddie: First kv_diff run (after vocab_shift) — avg token offset 0.05, max 1. snippet:
```
step 12: offset 1, step 140: offset 0, avg_logit_l2: 0.0042
```

vikram: Suggest we gate Dedicated rollouts until we confirm no quality regression. Configure a small canary with strict ROUGE sanity checks.

eva: Agreed — marking onboarding ticket as `onhold` and adding the failing prompts to the regression set. I'll open a tracking issue.

maddie: OK will follow up with asym+scale results in ~30m. Thanks all.
